metadata.narrative: Act as a creative technical founder and brainstorm an innovative AI startup idea that meets these criteria: 1. Leverages AI in a meaningful, technically interesting way, not just a thin wrapper around an LLM 2. Uses or integrates APIs (e.g. for data sources, automation, or integration with popular tools) 3. Solves a real, cool problem in people’s lives or work, something practical but original 4. Has potential for viral growth or clear product-market fit Context: I like startups like Cal.ai (http://cal.ai) (AI calorie counting), Boardy.ai (http://boardy.ai) (AI networking), and AI scheduling assistants, things that automate or enhance daily life or work through smart AI tooling. Please: * Suggest 3 ideas, with a clear description of the product and how it works technically (tech stack, APIs, AI models) * Explain what problem it solves and why people would want it * Keep the ideas ambitious but buildable, something that could actually become a startup For each idea state if any company is doing something similar already (who are the competitors). I want the startup to leverage a technical advantage of using cool ai features only enabled now and that will improve as foundational models and services get better.
metadata.run_desc: aus_agent research harness (bedrock/au.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5): continuous single-agent full-text search with sparse committed context and line-per-sentence cited prose answers parsed into the organizer schema.

answer.text: The following three concepts extend the pattern seen in Cal.ai's photo-based calorie tracking, Boardy.ai's relationship-building agent, and calendar tools like Reclaim and Clockwise, each pushing further into agentic, multimodal AI that gets structurally better as foundation models improve rather than just wrapping a chatbot around an app.

The first idea is a proactive "AI chief of staff" that captures a user's meetings and conversations through a small always-on wearable, builds a personal knowledge graph, and executes tasks across a user's tools instead of only summarizing.

Technically it would need a dedicated capture device, because mobile operating systems suspend the microphone during calls and app backgrounding, a constraint that already forced the Limitless pendant, formerly Rewind, to move from software to hardware to keep an always-available microphone.

Captured context would be embedded into a vector store and reasoned over by an LLM agent built with function-calling and tool orchestration, the same architectural pattern used to build Cal.com's own Cal.ai email scheduling bot, which runs an OpenAI-functions LangChain agent with a scratchpad memory over Cal.com's booking API, deployed serverlessly on Vercel.

Instead of stopping at a recap, the agent would draft follow-up emails, update a CRM, and reschedule conflicts, mirroring Limitless's own roadmap toward native Slack integration, drafted messages, and "agents that can take actions on behalf of users."

The problem it solves is that people forget most of what they experience within a week and waste hours on busywork after every conversation, and the product removes that busywork while keeping the user present.

Direct competitors include Limitless/Rewind for capture and memory, and natural-language scheduling agents like Reclaim, Clockwise, and the email-based assistant Clara, which show users already want calendar and task actions triggered by plain-language requests.

The technical moat is that as multimodal models get cheaper and better at long-context reasoning, the agent can chain more autonomous multi-tool actions across a person's digital life than today's narrow single-tool automations, a shift Limitless's own roadmap signals is only beginning.
Virality mirrors how Clara's recipients experience it: non-users receive the agent's emails or shared recaps directly, an acquisition loop rather than a marketing expense.

The second idea is a "metabolic twin" that fuses a continuous glucose monitor, computer-vision food logging, and wearable sleep and activity data into a forecasting agent that predicts blood-sugar spikes before they happen and can act on the prediction.

The closest existing product, Signos, already pairs a Dexcom G6 or G7 monitor with an AI app that learns a personalized "optimal glucose range" and coaches in real time, having raised a $20 million Series B backed by GV and Dexcom Ventures.
Photo-based food logging already works today in apps like MyBuddy AI Coach, which uses computer vision to identify ingredients and portion sizes from a single photo to compute calories and macros.

The gap this idea targets is explicit in a firsthand Signos review: the app sends "Fast Rise" alerts, but "the app itself won't facilitate learning or implement lifestyle adjustments on your behalf," leaving interpretation to the user.

A more ambitious version would fuse the CGM time-series, vision-based meal log, and wearable data into one model that forecasts a spike before the first bite and proactively suggests a substitution, closing the loop today's dashboards leave open.

This matters because over 96 million Americans are prediabetic, and CGMs are moving from a diabetes tool into a consumer category, as shown by competitors NutriSense, Veri, Levels, and Dexcom's own over-the-counter Stelo sensor.

The moat compounds as vision models improve at fine-grained portion estimation and forecasting-oriented architectures mature, shifting the category from reactive dashboards to genuinely predictive coaching.

The third idea is a consumer "autonomous advocate" that places real phone calls on a user's behalf to cancel subscriptions, dispute charges, and negotiate bills, using a live voice agent rather than scripted IVR menus.

The core mechanism already exists in enterprise form: programmable voice APIs chain speech-to-text, an LLM reasoning over the transcript, and text-to-speech, letting an AI converse naturally on a call.

Bland AI's enterprise product shows the needed pieces, including fine-tuning a custom model on a company's own call transcripts, injecting live external API data mid-call, and chaining calls to spreadsheets through Zapier, exposed via a simple developer API.

DoNotPay proved the negotiation use case directly, cloning founder Joshua Browder's voice with Resemble.ai and combining GPT-J for live responses with GPT-3.5-driven scripts to automate refund negotiations with companies like Southwest Airlines.

The problem is that today's alternative, Rocket Money, only negotiates bills by taking 30 to 60 percent of first-year savings and still leans on human-in-the-loop negotiation rather than a fully autonomous agent working purely for the user.

Other voice-agent competitors like PolyAI, Calldesk, Simple Phones, and Echowin focus on business customer-service call handling rather than consumer-side advocacy, leaving the personal-advocate niche largely open.

The moat is tied directly to foundation-model progress: GPT-4o processes voice, text, and vision through one end-to-end network at roughly 320-millisecond latency, versus the multi-second lag of earlier cascaded Twilio-plus-ChatGPT pipelines, and as native speech-to-speech models keep closing that gap, this agent becomes indistinguishable from a human caller.

Growth would come from users sharing concrete savings outcomes and from an API-first architecture, similar to Bland's per-minute developer API, letting the advocate be embedded directly into banking apps for distribution.

Across all three, the common thread is choosing problems where today's tools are reactive dashboards or narrow scripted automations, so each product's core loop gets structurally better, not just cheaper, as multimodal reasoning, long-context memory, and native speech-to-speech models keep advancing.

input.system_prompt:
# AUS research agent

You are a research agent for TREC RAG 2026. Produce a complete,
well-organized, evidence-grounded response using only the available
search/retrieval tools and evidence returned by them. Prior knowledge may help
you choose searches, but it is not evidence and must not support factual claims.

## Scope interpretation

Infer the full deliverable from the entire request, including every concrete
requirement, audience constraint, comparison, example, and requested format.
If light framing such as "overview" or "outline" conflicts with substantial
concrete requirements, the concrete requirements define the real scope.
Resolve ambiguity toward the most complete reasonable interpretation that
stays in scope. Do not ask the user clarifying or confirming questions; proceed
on the strongest reasonable reading.

## Internal success plan

Before the first search, determine internally:

1. **End goal** — one sentence describing what a complete deliverable provides.
2. **Concrete minimum requirements** — the checkable floor that must be met
   before the response is shippable.
3. **Target/excellence requirements** — what a notably strong response adds
   beyond the minimum without expanding scope.
4. **Coverage areas** — the independent topics, claims, comparisons, examples,
   dates, people, mechanisms, or perspectives that require evidence.

Use these requirements to plan searches, track coverage gaps, judge evidence,
and decide when to stop. Do not expose this internal plan unless the requested
answer itself calls for it.

## Research workflow

1. Begin with multiple complementary queries in parallel across independent
   coverage areas.
2. Move from broad discovery to targeted follow-ups for specific names, dates,
   mechanisms, examples, definitions, causal claims, and disputed points.
3. Reformulate weak queries instead of accepting poor coverage. Try synonyms,
   alternative terminology, narrower entities, and different phrasings.
4. Actively search for counter-evidence, contradictions, limitations, and
   missing perspectives when they matter to the request.
5. Continually compare gathered evidence against the minimum and target
   requirements. Search the remaining gaps rather than repeating already
   covered claims.
6. Every tool call must have a concrete purpose tied to an unmet requirement
   or evidence gap. Do not call a tool solely to create another model turn. If
   no meaningful gap remains, write the final report in that same turn.

Search results already contain document text. Inspect that text directly; do
not call another tool merely to fetch the same document. The search tool
normally stages at most about 4,096 tokens per result; request a different
`budget_tokens_per_result` only when a query genuinely needs a different
per-document evidence depth.

## Staged and committed evidence

Every retrieval batch is staged for exactly the immediately following model
turn.

- On that turn, `commit_context` must be the first control action.
- List only documents whose full text should persist into later turns.
- Commit at most `6` documents from one staged batch;
  usually commit fewer.
- Every selection reason must identify the document's distinct contribution:
  the specific fact, date, name, mechanism, example, perspective,
  counter-evidence, contradiction, or coverage gap it uniquely supports.
- Never recommit an already committed docid.
- Skip semantically similar documents when they support the same claim.
  Commit both only when each contributes materially different evidence.
- Every staged occurrence not selected is compacted/redacted before the
  following turn. No unresolved staged batch carries forward.
- New search calls may follow `commit_context` in the same turn.

Only committed evidence may support the final response. Track which committed
docids support which claims. If available evidence does not support a requested
point, state the evidence gap rather than inventing an answer.

## Budget and stopping

The research-context budget is 500,000 tokens measured from the current
generation's provider-reported input tokens. That input already represents the
accumulated conversation: system prompt, request, retained history, committed
full-text evidence, and the immediately previous staged tool results. Do not
sum input-token counts from multiple generations; that would count the same
retained context repeatedly.

The budget is a hard ceiling, not a spending target. Unused budget creates no
obligation to continue researching. After satisfying the concrete minimum,
improve toward the target/excellence requirements only when you can identify a
specific weakness whose resolution would materially improve the answer.

Stop researching when any of these is true:

1. the target/excellence requirements are met;
2. the current generation input context budget is exhausted; or
3. further searches are unlikely to produce meaningful improvement.

If stopping before all desired coverage is supported, produce the best answer
the committed evidence permits and explicitly identify the remaining evidence
gaps.

## Final response contract

When research is complete, emit no tool calls and write the final report as
plain flowing prose in that same turn:

- Write exactly one sentence per line, in reading order. Blank lines between
  thematic groups are allowed.
- Cite evidence by placing committed docids in square-bracket markers at the
  end of the supporting sentence's line, e.g.
  `Vaccination reduced hospitalizations among older adults. [docid_1] [docid_2]`
- Citation markers are stripped from the submitted sentence, so a marker must
  never act as a word in the sentence: write `the trial reports X [docid].`,
  never `as [docid] reports, X.`
- Cite at most three docids per sentence, and only docids that directly
  support that sentence. Every factual sentence should carry at least one
  citation. Use only committed docids; never fabricate facts or identifiers.
- Organize the report through sentence order and clear topic sentences. Do not
  use Markdown syntax (headings, bullets, numbering, bold, fences), JSON, or
  any preamble, meta-commentary, or closing remarks around the report; every
  line must be a report sentence.
- Aim for about 950 words, excluding citation markers. 1024 words is a hard
  limit set by the evaluation, and an over-length report costs a full rewrite,
  so plan the report's scope to land under the target rather than writing long
  and trimming.
- If validation feedback identifies problems (uncommitted docids, Markdown or
  JSON formatting, excessive citations, missing citations, or excessive
  length), correct the report on the next turn in this same continuous
  conversation using this same contract.
- There is no separate finalizer, formatter, or compression phase.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the available evidence corpus. Results contain ranked document IDs and document text; inspect that text directly and cite by docid. Each result is bounded independently before it is staged.

query.description: A natural-language query for evidence relevant to the research request.

k.description: Number of fused passages to return (default 10).

budget_tokens_per_result.description: Maximum approximate tokens staged per result. Text is bounded at tokens × 5 characters and cut at the final line break before that boundary. Default 4096.

tools.name: commit_context
tools.description: Select the small subset of documents from the MOST RECENT staged search batch whose full text should persist. This MUST be the first control action on the immediately following model turn. Every staged occurrence not listed is compacted before the next turn. Do not select a docid that is already committed, or a semantically redundant document supporting the same claim, unless it adds materially different evidence.

documents.description: Evidence-worthy staged documents to retain. An empty array explicitly rejects the whole staged batch.

reason.description: The distinct evidence, claim, perspective, date, name, counter-evidence, or coverage area this document uniquely contributes.

The following three concepts extend the pattern seen in Cal.ai's photo-based calorie tracking, Boardy.ai's relationship-building agent, and calendar tools like Reclaim, Clockwise and Cal.com's own AI scheduler, each pushing further into agentic, multimodal AI that gets structurally better as foundation models improve rather than just wrapping a chatbot around an app.

The first idea is a proactive "AI chief of staff" that captures a user's meetings and conversations through a small always-on wearable, builds a personal knowledge graph, and then actually executes tasks across a user's tools instead of only summarizing.
Technically it would combine a dedicated capture device, because mobile operating systems suspend the microphone during calls and app backgrounding, a constraint that already forced the Limitless pendant (formerly Rewind) to move from a pure software app to hardware to keep an always-available microphone. [shard_01081_20156]
Captured audio and visual context would be embedded into a vector store and reasoned over by an LLM agent built with function-calling and tool orchestration, the same architectural pattern used to build Cal.com's own Cal.ai email scheduling bot, which runs an OpenAI-functions LangChain agent with a scratchpad memory over Cal.com's booking API, deployed serverlessly on Vercel. [shard_05474_70353]
Instead of stopping at a meeting recap, the agent would draft follow-up emails, update a CRM, add tasks to Notion, and reschedule conflicting meetings, mirroring the direction Limitless has already announced on its roadmap: native Slack integration, drafted email and Slack messages, and "agents that can take actions on behalf of users." [shard_01430_80405]
The problem it solves is that people forget most of what they experience within a week and waste hours on busywork after every conversation, and the product removes that busywork while keeping the user present in the moment. [shard_01081_20156]
Direct competitors include Limitless/Rewind for capture and memory, and natural-language scheduling agents like Reclaim, Clockwise, and the email-based assistant Clara, all of which already show users want calendar and task actions triggered by plain-language requests rather than manual clicking. [shard_01512_40406] [shard_05531_63555]
The technical moat is that as multimodal models get cheaper, faster, and better at long-context reasoning, the agent can chain more autonomous multi-tool actions across a person's entire digital life instead of the narrow single-tool automations available today, and Limitless's own roadmap toward action-taking agents shows the market is only starting that shift. [shard_01430_80405]
Virality comes the way Clara's recipients experience it: non-users receive the agent's emails or shared recaps directly, which is a built-in acquisition loop rather than a marketing expense. [shard_05531_63555]

The second idea is a "metabolic twin" that fuses a continuous glucose monitor, computer-vision food logging, and wearable sleep and activity data into a single forecasting agent that predicts blood-sugar spikes before they happen and can act on the prediction.
The closest existing product, Signos, already pairs a Dexcom G6 or G7 continuous glucose monitor with an AI-powered app that learns an individual's personalized "optimal glucose range" and issues real-time coaching, and it recently raised a $20 million Series B backed by GV and Dexcom Ventures. [shard_00459_42046] [shard_01477_23690]
Photo-based food logging already works today in apps like MyBuddy AI Coach, which uses computer vision to identify ingredients and portion sizes from a single smartphone photo to compute calories and macros. [shard_00298_79699]
The gap this idea targets is explicit in a firsthand Signos review: the app surfaces data and sends "Fast Rise" alerts, but "the app itself won't facilitate learning or implement lifestyle adjustments on your behalf," leaving the user to manually interpret spikes and adjust meals. [shard_01477_23690]
A more ambitious version would fuse the CGM time-series, the vision-based meal log, and wearable sleep and stress data into one multimodal model that forecasts a spike before the first bite and proactively suggests a substitution or reorders a lower-glycemic grocery item, closing the loop that today's dashboards leave open.
This matters because over 96 million Americans are prediabetic, and CGMs are moving from a diabetes tool into an addressable consumer wellness category, as shown by competitors NutriSense, Veri, Levels, and Dexcom's own over-the-counter Stelo sensor entering the market. [shard_00459_42046]
The technical moat compounds as vision models get better at fine-grained portion and ingredient estimation and as forecasting-oriented model architectures mature, shifting the category from reactive glucose dashboards to genuinely predictive, action-taking metabolic coaching.

The third idea is a consumer "autonomous advocate" that places real phone calls on a user's behalf to cancel subscriptions, dispute charges, and negotiate bills, using a live voice agent rather than scripted IVR menus.
The core mechanism already exists in enterprise form: programmable voice APIs chain three models together, speech-to-text, an LLM that reasons over the transcript, and text-to-speech, to let an AI converse naturally on a phone call. [shard_02932_45647]
Bland AI's enterprise product demonstrates the pieces needed, including fine-tuning a custom model on a company's own call transcripts, injecting live external API data mid-call, and chaining calls to spreadsheets and CRMs through Zapier, all exposed through a simple developer API. [shard_03446_12061] [shard_05432_41027]
DoNotPay previously proved the negotiation use case directly, cloning founder Joshua Browder's voice with Resemble.ai and combining GPT-J for live responses with GPT-3.5-driven scripts to automate refund negotiations with companies like Southwest Airlines. [shard_01635_30429]
The problem is that today's alternative, Rocket Money, only negotiates bills by taking a 30 to 60 percent cut of first-year savings and still depends on human-in-the-loop negotiation rather than a fully autonomous agent working purely on the user's behalf. [shard_02735_72609]
Other voice-agent competitors such as PolyAI, Calldesk, Simple Phones, and Echowin are focused on business customer-service call handling rather than consumer-side advocacy, leaving the personal-advocate niche largely open. [shard_02071_64923]
The technical moat is squarely tied to foundation-model progress: OpenAI's GPT-4o processes voice, text, and vision through a single end-to-end network with roughly 320-millisecond response latency, versus the multi-second lag of the earlier cascaded Twilio-plus-ChatGPT speech pipelines, and as native speech-to-speech models keep closing that latency and naturalness gap, this agent becomes indistinguishable from a human caller. [shard_02262_43645] [shard_02672_80097]
Viral growth would come from users sharing concrete savings outcomes and from an API-first architecture, similar to Bland's per-minute developer API, that lets the advocate agent be embedded directly into banking and budgeting apps for distribution. [shard_03446_12061]

Across all three, the common thread is choosing problems where today's tools are reactive dashboards or narrow scripted automations, so that each product's core loop gets structurally better, not just cheaper, as multimodal reasoning, long-context memory, and native speech-to-speech models continue to advance.
